chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us: He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatam narrated to us: He said: Al-Ala' ibn Salim narrated to us: He said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. Shari'k informed us, from Sammak, and Abd Allah ibn Umayr, and Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: We heard Jabir ibn Samurah saying: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with my father, so he said: 'This nation will not cease to be good, their affair manifest over their enemies, until twelve kings pass, or he said: twelve Caliphs.' Then he said a word that was hidden from me, so I asked my father, who said: He said: 'They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve caliphs mentioned in the hadith and what is their lineage?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Jabir ibn Samurah establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve divinely appointed successors, a core tenet in Shia eschatology that ensures the continuity of authentic leadership. The Prophet’s assurance that the community’s affairs will remain 'manifest' and victorious until their succession underscores the theological link between legitimate authority and communal stability. While the text specifies Quraysh, Shia scholarship traditionally identifies these twelve as the Prophet’s progeny, beginning with Imam Ali (AS), thereby distinguishing them from the broader historical caliphs.
